title: kith-chat + kith-attach: strengths
description: Strong points in kith-chat and kith-attach: (1) BlobStore validate_blob_id is thorough — rejects empty, dot-leading, slash, backslash, null, space, too-long, and non-alphanumeric IDs; blob_exists validates before path construction. (2) write_blob and write_blob_streaming both use atomic temp-file-then-rename pattern with unique per-write nonces to prevent concurrent write collisions. Cleanup on error (remove_file after sync_all or write_all failure) is correct. (3) old_state capture inside the first lock scope prevents sinceState drift from concurrent writes in all three set handlers — the design is intentional and well-commented. (4) maxChanges=0 returns invalidArguments rather than silently returning empty results, matching the RFC SHOULD as a MUST. (5) Attachment validation pipeline (blobId format, existence, filename path-traversal checks, content-type slash count, size range, sha256 format) is defense-in-depth at the right layer. (6) Group-chat fanout uses all-or-nothing delivery: if any member has no mailbox host the send fails rather than silently dropping members. (7) Test coverage is strong: unit tests use independent oracles from RFC spec, integration tests exercise multi-step workflows, boundary tests cover exact MAX_BODY_BYTES values, auth rejection tests verify both directions (peer cannot call owner methods AND owner cannot call peer methods).
